transcript.content: Hello, nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because I'm having a really hard time stopping my thoughts. Once a worry starts—whether it's about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or just wondering if I missed something at work—I just can't seem to shelve it in my mind. 

It doesn't matter how many lists I make or how hard I try to redirect myself to something else. I just can't seem to let these things go once they pop into my head.
How long have you been dealing with this persistent worrying?
It's been going on for about a year and two months now. Um, it really started right around the time my mother moved into my home after she had a fall.
Do you find yourself feeling driven to repeat certain actions or rituals, like checking things over and over, in order to relieve that worry?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I mean, I look at the lists I make, but I don't feel forced to check things over and over, or do any kind of rituals. It's really just the thoughts themselves that get stuck in my head, not so much any physical actions I feel like I have to do.
Have you noticed any persistent muscle tension or physical tightness in your body since this worrying started?

Yes, definitely. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders just feel... locked up, I guess, from bracing myself all the time. And I actually catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, especially when I'm answering work emails or just sitting there listening to see if my mother is moving around in the next room.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep or waking up frequently?

Yes, I have. Most nights, I just lie there replaying the day in my head, um, planning for every possible problem that might come up. And then... well, if I do manage to fall asleep and wake up because I hear my mother moving around, I'm usually up for an hour or two after that. By the time I arrive at the library for work in the morning, I just feel like I never really rested at all.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, keyed up, or on edge?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have that muscle tightness I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I feel restless or jittery. I don't really have trouble sitting still or anything like that. It's mostly just the worrying going on in my head, rather than feeling physically keyed up.
Have you found yourself becoming easily fatigued or feeling worn out more quickly than usual?

No, not really. I mean, I feel tired in the mornings because of my sleep, like I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I get worn out more quickly during the day. I can still get through my shifts at the library and do what I need to do at home without feeling easily fatigued. It's really just the lack of sleep making me tired, not getting exhausted from doing things.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or having a shorter temper than usual?

No, um, I haven't really noticed that. I don't think I've been snapping at anyone at work or at home. Even with being tired from the lack of sleep, my temper is pretty much the same as it's always been. I wouldn't say I'm irritable at all.
Have you had any trouble concentrating on tasks or felt like your mind goes blank?

Yes, actually, I have noticed that. It happens at work a lot. During cataloging reviews, or even in staff meetings, I'll be looking right at my computer screen or the meeting agenda, and then I suddenly realize my mind just... went totally blank. I haven't absorbed a single word. It's like my brain just wanders off and starts fixating on some problem I feel like I should have prevented, and I completely lose focus on what's right in front of me.
